reasoning: The code path is real. XAIWireTypes.swift:261 copies creditUsagePercent into utilizationPercent without clamping, at L268-271. UsageWindow.swift:14-20 stores it as is. UsageSnapshot.swift:70-72 takes the max. UsageStore.swift:379/156 publishes it. MenuBarLabelView.swift:41 then runs Int(percent.rounded()), which would trap on 1e300. The alleged security damage does not hold, though. The only party who can put that value in the payload is the first-party HTTPS endpoint the user already trusts and is authenticated to (cli-chat-proxy.grok.com, XAIProvider.swift:7/50). TLS rules out a network attacker. What the 'attacker' gets is a crash of the user's own read-only display app. It exposes no data, grants no write or code execution, and crosses no privilege boundary. A vendor that wanted to break the card could just stop serving data. What remains is a robustness bug: a malformed vendor response crashes the app, and the cache can make the crash come back after relaunch. The fix is still worth doing: check isFinite and clamp in UsageWindow.init. As written, though, the finding claims attacker-driven DoS and assumes a hostile source, so it is not a security impact.
